blocks.text: When a civil servant in Abuja is paid, the naira does not travel as a sack of notes from the Ministry of Finance. It appears as a balance at a commercial bank, which then lends most of it to a trader in Onitsha. That chain — deposit, reserve, loan — is how Nigerian banks create credit, and it is why the Central Bank of Nigeria can slow or speed the whole system by changing one ratio.

blocks.markdown:
**Commercial banks** are profit-seeking firms that accept deposits and grant loans. Their everyday functions include keeping current, savings and time accounts; making loans and overdrafts; discounting bills; arranging payments at home and abroad; providing safe custody and standing orders; and advising customers. The function that matters most for the money supply is **credit creation**.

Banks need keep only a fraction of deposits as cash or balances at the CBN — the **cash reserve ratio (CRR)**. The rest can be lent. A loan credited to a borrower's account becomes a new deposit in the system, which supports a further loan, and so on. The **credit multiplier** is $1/\text{cash ratio}$. If the ratio is 10 per cent, ₦1 of new deposits can support ₦10 of total deposits in the limiting case.

blocks.title: Credit creation
blocks.text: The process by which commercial banks expand loans, and therefore deposits, by a multiple of an initial cash deposit, subject to the cash reserve ratio. Additional credit created equals initial deposit × (1 − r)/r, where r is the cash ratio. Leakages, excess reserves and a lack of willing borrowers all cut the actual multiple below this theoretical maximum.

blocks.title: Maximum additional credit from a new deposit
blocks.prompt: A customer lodges ₦50,000 in a commercial bank. The cash reserve ratio set by the CBN is 10 per cent. Calculate the credit multiplier, the maximum total deposits that can be supported, and the maximum additional credit the banking system can create.

steps.text: The credit multiplier is the reciprocal of the cash ratio.
Maximum total deposits equal the initial deposit times the multiplier.
The bank must keep 10 per cent of ₦50,000, that is ₦5,000, as cash. The first loan is therefore ₦45,000.
Additional credit created is total deposits minus the original deposit.
The same figure comes from initial deposit × (1 − r)/r = ₦50,000 × 9 = ₦450,000. In practice leakages into cash and excess reserves make the actual expansion smaller.

blocks.answer: Multiplier 10; maximum deposits ₦500,000; maximum additional credit ₦450,000

blocks.markdown:
### Functions of the Central Bank of Nigeria

The CBN is the apex monetary authority. It is **banker to the federal government** (holding the Treasury’s accounts, managing debt issues and making payments). It is **banker to the banks** and **lender of last resort** when a solvent bank is short of cash. It has the **sole right of note issue** — only the CBN may print the naira. It **supervises** banks and other financial institutions, manages the country’s foreign reserves and advises the government on economic policy.

Its most examined tools of **monetary policy** are:

- **CRR** — raising the cash ratio forces banks to lend less.
- **MPR (Monetary Policy Rate)** — the benchmark interest rate; a higher MPR makes borrowing dearer.
- **OMO (Open Market Operations)** — selling Treasury bills withdraws naira from the banks; buying them injects naira.
- Liquidity ratio, moral suasion and special deposits are supporting instruments.

blocks.title: NDIC
blocks.text: The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation insures depositors’ funds up to a stated limit if a licensed bank fails. The scheme exists to protect small savers and to stop a run on one bank from spreading to the rest of the system. It is not a commercial bank and it does not create credit.

blocks.title: Credit created is not the same as total deposits
blocks.text: If the question asks for **additional credit**, subtract the original deposit after applying the multiplier. If it asks for **total deposits** (or the maximum amount of money that can be created), leave the original deposit in. Read the wording twice before you multiply.

points: Commercial banks accept deposits, grant loans and create credit by lending a multiple of cash reserves.
The credit multiplier is 1/cash ratio; additional credit = deposit × (1 − r)/r, reduced in practice by leakages.
The CBN is banker to government and to banks, sole issuer of the naira, supervisor of banks and the operator of monetary policy (CRR, MPR, OMO).
NDIC insures deposits to protect savers and financial stability.
The money market deals in short-term instruments such as Treasury bills; the capital market, centred on the NGX, deals in shares and long-term bonds.
